messages:
sara: Heads-up: noticed dashboard hydration stalls right after the LZ4 runtime bump. small charts pause ~350ms on first view. anyone else? :frowning:
ben: saw it in canary. profiler shows synchronous import of `perf/collector` during widget init. looks like an eager telemetry wire got pulled into the chart entry chunk.
tim: hmm we purposely inlined a tiny helper in chart-core last week to shave 5ms, but it imported `perf/collector` for an early ping. that helper expanded into a full collector library in the packaged output.
release-bot: deploy "web-client@2026.03.23-lz4-runtime" finished 2026-03-23T04:12:12Z (canary 12%).
perf-bot: alert: LCP 75th percentile increased by 310ms for canary cohort at 04:20 UTC.
sara: two things compounding: 1) eager telemetry increased parse time and 2) router prefetch kicks off multiple widget hydration concurrently, causing a thundering parse effect.
ben: short-term mitigations: a) revert the helper in chart-core b) replace eager import with deferred dynamic import c) throttle widget hydration concurrency to 2 via feature flag.
tim: I can push a tiny hotfix that switches to:
```
// defer collector
setTimeout(() => import('./perf/collector').then(m => m.init()), 0)
```
and add `/* webpackChunkName: "perf-collector" */` to force a separate chunk.
infra: I'll flip the prefetch concurrency flag to 2 for canary groups once hotfix is live.
ben: also add a CI bundle-delta check: fail if any chart splitpoint grows >150KB gz. prevents regressions like this.
sara: graceful approach for product: if we delay collector, we lose a handful of early metrics used for rollout gating. can we send a tiny synchronous beacon for the rollout ping only, then load the collector async?
tim: yes. minimal sync ping:
```
navigator.sendBeacon('/r/early-ping', JSON.stringify({rid: window.RAW_RID}))
```
then load collector later. lightweight and meets rollout requirement.
release-bot: canary scale adjusted per request.
sara: plan: tim cut hotfix PR, infra throttle concurrency, run perf smoke on staging, then resume canary. we'll follow up with RFC on telemetry initialization semantics. thanks all. :thumbsup:
